articles.title: Auditing Chatbots for Incursion into Professional Legal Practice
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The provision of legal advice has long been in the exclusive jurisdiction of licensed attorneys-a boundary that unauthorized practice of law (UPL) doctrine maintains to protect the public from incompetent counsel. We argue that this boundary is being redrawn, not by courts or bar authorities, but by frontier AI companies. articles.title: DOCKET: A Pluralistic Benchmark for Evaluating AI-Assisted Policy Feedback in U.S. Rulemaking
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI models advance and impact deliberative democracies, there is a growing need to assess their support of pluralistic viewpoints. Most pluralism benchmarks are insufficient for this: they are not grounded in diversity (i.e., stakeholders across different frames, skills and needs), quality (i.e., rigorous and technical debates), and impact (i.e., invested deliberators and real-world outcomes). articles.title: Measuring Public Participation in Local Government: An Audio-Based Instrument for Classifying Speakers in City Council Meetings
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much does the public actually speak in local government? Despite sustained interest in democratic participation, we lack large-scale measures of public voice at the local level, because the underlying record -- audio of open meetings -- has been prohibitively costly to convert into data. articles.title: Large language models put existential risk from artificial intelligence at 10%
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How likely is it that advanced artificial intelligence (AI) will cause human extinction or a similarly permanent disempowerment of humanity? Humans, including AI experts, frequently disagree on this question. Yet one important perspective is missing from this debate: that of AI systems themselves. We put the question to 241 large language models (LLMs) at every available reasoning setting. The models converged on a median risk of 10.0%, with the middle 90% of their estimates between 3.5% and 15.8%, far narrower than the spread among human experts

articles.title: Efficiency Gains in Social Science Research: A Prospective Silicon Sampling Protocol for Pre-Treatment and Code Optimization
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study evaluates the methodological potential of using large language models (LLMs) to generate synthetic datasets prior to real-world data collection, thereby streamlining subsequent processing and statistical analysis. The approach is applied to a survey conducted within the France Life Imaging (FLI) network, leveraging three distinct LLMs (Sonnet 4.6, GPT 5.3, and Kimi 2.6) to simulate responses and prepare data processing workflows. articles.title: Accounting for Trust and Safety: Bounding Content-Moderation Quality from Records You Already Hold
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Platforms use expert audits to measure content-moderation quality. This paper develops a formal method for checking those claims using records platforms already maintain, such as appeal reversals and confirmed reports. These records provide one-sided bounds: they can show that a stated quality target was missed, but cannot prove that it was met. The paper presents the theory, limitations, constructed examples, and a prospective protocol for future evaluation. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The EU AI Act imposes technical and organizational requirements for high-risk AI systems, but applying these requirements involves contextual choices about what to measure and what evidence supports a compliance claim. articles.title: Measured from the feed: the unsustainable growth of AI video generation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-video generation runs at commercial scale, but its broader environmental impacts remain, to our knowledge, understudied. Providers rarely disclose video volumes or energy needs; we measured the yearly video output of two commercial platforms and built a prospective model of such services' absolute footprint from training to storage. Our projections suggest that reducing emissions depends on both limiting growth in video generation and achieving substantial efficiency gains. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17953v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We argue that the Transformer revolution is not adequately understood as a merely quantitative expansion of deep learning, but as the emergence of a new paradigm based on a different principle of inference.
